messages.subject: predicting outcomes from a negative binomial model (Rstan
parts:
Hi All,

I am currently working on a negative binomial model. I was able to get the coefficients for the NB model  using the attached script. Next, I would like to predict crashes (dependent variable) using the developed NB model. I don't know how I can implement that in RStan. 

I will appreciate any help.

Thanks.

parts:
On Friday, September 30, 2016 at 11:53:28 AM UTC-4, malai...@gmail.com wrote:
I am currently working on a negative binomial model. I was able to get the coefficients for the NB model  using the attached script. Next, I would like to predict crashes (dependent variable) using the developed NB model. I don't know how I can implement that in RStan.

There is a neg_binomial_2_rng() function that you can call in the generated quantities block. However, it will often fail during the warmup phase causing the chains to stop, in which case you would be better off calling rnbinom() in R after you have draws of the betas.
I will appreciate any help.

There is little reason to write GLMs like this yourself. The stan_glm.nb() function in rstanarm will do this model, will do this model better if you specify QR = TRUE, is more integrated with both shinystan and loo, and has a posterior_predict() function that predicts the outcome based on the posterior (possibly with new data on the predictors).

Ben

parts:
You just need to do the same thing with the site variables.

And I'd highly suggest containers rather than hard-coded numbers.

This is almost certainly going to be a problem:

> phi ~ cauchy(0.001,0.001);


Is that an attempted hack for something? Is there a way to rescale
phi to be on the unit scale?

We also don't recommend priors like these

> beta3 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);

that put a lot of prior mass on values with absolute value > 1e4.

- Bob
